en.title: Maximum Chalk Difference Sum Preserving the Adjacent Up/Down Pattern
en.description: Ramu and Sonu each have N chalks with pairwise distinct lengths. Sonu may rearrange his chalks, but every pair of adjacent positions must keep the same strict up/down direction as the corresponding positions of Ramu's chalks. Find the maximum sum of the absolute length differences between Sonu's adjacent chalks.
en.input: The first line contains N (this site's range: 1≤N≤14). The second line contains N positive integers, the lengths of Ramu's chalks; the third line contains N positive integers, the lengths of Sonu's chalks. The lengths within each group are distinct.
en.output: Output the maximum sum of absolute differences that satisfies the adjacent up/down pattern.
en.explanation: Use a bitmask to represent the chalks already placed, with the last chalk as part of the state; match Ramu's up/down relations position by position and maximize the total difference.
hints: The direction at each position is determined by how Ramu's adjacent lengths compare.
The subset and the last value are enough to describe the transition boundary of a completed prefix.
With N≤14, all subset states can be kept to find the exact optimum.
